t:
Many have heard stories about the Silent Hills. An ancient evil awoke in that land, turning the peasants into will-less ghosts. They wandered their lands until brave heroes put an end to their suffering.

But in the deep layers of the Astral the Silent Hills have a reflection. It was this that an imperial Warlock chose for his experiments. And he got so carried away that the horrors of old now seem like a children's fairy tale. The villain destroyed the whole people and turned the good inhabitants into an army of the undead. Those hills are Silent no longer, but Dead!

Bosses: Cadaver, Guardian, Murderess, Sarang Fravashi.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

t: This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, an oligarch and inventor. He is a rich and famous man, but not much respected: he is far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only this last time he picked the wrong target: he had the nerve to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker would not swallow the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. Nothing came of it, I think: the imperial soldiers are strong, but a factory stuffed to the rafters with weapons can't be taken in one rush either. We Leaguers have nothing to do there — except perhaps watch the show from afar. Want to make a bet? I wager ten gold that the Imperials won't manage it!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to search for Yelisseus Korolev. And only his old nanny knew where he was. It turned out that Yelisseus had disappeared on the Death Plant island: he had gone there to learn from Nomarkh Iblis, the Oligarch, where to find his beloved Annette. Setting off after Yelisseus, the heroes met on the island Leila Snoop, a Committee operative who had picked up the trail of a sinister conspiracy.

This very Nomarkh Iblis, one of the seven Oligarchs who rule the Free Traders, grew rich on the arms trade. All those turrets, mechanisms and other weapons that have flooded Sarnaut in recent years are his handiwork. But the trouble lay elsewhere. Not long ago Iblis put a new weapon on sale — the Spinners. And on every one of the Spinners he installed a remote-control device. At one fine moment the Spinners were to rise against their owners, and Iblis would become the ruler of all Sarnaut. Leila offered to thwart his plans. Long and bloody was the path through the laboratories and workshops of the Death Plant; the Xadaganian scout herself fell victim (or so it seemed at the time); and Yelisseus was found, whom Iblis had wanted to turn into a mechanical bogatyr. For it turned out that all of Catherina's guard, the bogatyrs, had been remade from heroes, and inside the mechanical bodies were the Sparks of the living. The heroes fought their way out of the dungeons with Yelisseus, finished off Iblis himself, and on his body found documents proving that he had been cooperating with Catherina. She did not deny it, and admitted that she had needed Iblis for his technologies. "Engineers with powerful manatrons, a flying tower, the best shipyard in the world and my mechanical guard — none of this came out of thin air."

Bosses: Yasskul Samekh, Modified Orc, Ghost of Yaver Khess, Polytoc Hexnut.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
The ancient city-state of Dersaadet is a true historical monument. Its beautiful squares and palaces keep the spirit of long-gone times.

This is exactly how the cities of the Xadagan Empire looked in that memorable time when the heroes of "Evil Islands" walked their streets.

Lost in the Astral, Dersaadet escaped the demon invasion and any part in the bloody war of the great factions. The local Xadaganians have never seen a mana pipeline and do not know Yasker, yet they cannot be called savages.

Any local architect could outdo the best masters of Sarnaut, and the grace of its maidens would make even elven dancers envious!

Alas, life prepared a cruel trial for the last sultan of Dersaadet. His only daughter would die on the day she came of age, poisoned by a snake's venom — so a Gypsy woman foretold. Unwilling to accept his fate, the ruler built an unreachable tower and hid his child in it. But on the girl's eighteenth birthday a sinister magical haze enveloped her refuge. The green mist took the shape of a huge snake coiled around the tower walls.

Soon rumors spread from the palace square that some misfortune had befallen the princess and that the lawful ruler of the city had vanished. Taking advantage of this, the unruly janizaries began to plunder the city they had sworn to protect.

It is said that behind it all stands the cunning Vizier — a great wizard and master of transformation.

Rumor has it that he isn't even a man, but a jinn who has taken mortal form. One way or another, traveling heroes will certainly have to face this powerful and domineering figure if they wish to shed light on the island's dark mystery.

For now the future of Dersaadet is hidden in mist even from the strongest oracles. Who knows, perhaps it is your party that will manage to get into the princess's tower? Whether you can save the unfortunate girl and win the coveted reward for it depends on you alone!

Bosses: Minotaur, Mehmet Pasha, Rajima, Lamia Princess.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Xadaganians.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What tricky questions you ask. And do you know that for that sort of thing you can end up in the Committee's dungeons? You see, even after the Cataclysm not all Xadaganians accepted Nezeb's rule. When the industrial revolution began in the Empire, some isolated allods inhabited by Xadaganians did not accept the new doctrine and went on living by the old customs. Dersaadet is just such a place. A shard, so to speak, of the old Empire, frozen in timelessness. There they do not believe in the Light, do not honour the saints of the Trinity Church, but pray to the Almighty in a mosque. Dersaadet is ruled by Sultan Mustapha al Muhad, and his power is boundless. And whoever wants to challenge it will have to deal with loyal janissaries and the magic of a cunning vizier. But if you come to Dersaadet in peace, generous hospitality awaits you, fine wines and delicacies such as the world has never seen!

Bosses: Minotaur, Mehmet Pasha, Rajima, Lamia Princess.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
What questions you ask! I'd gladly forget that island, but I can't...

Long ago Kanian druids brought a shoot of the Great Tree to a lifeless islet and turned the barren stone into a truly magnificent forest. I happened to visit it, and I confess without a word of a lie — even in the Empire there are few places whose beauty could compare with that wonderful sunny island as it was then. The mentor of the local pagans, the wise Dobroslav Radov, proved a most cordial Host and welcomed me, an Imperial, hospitably, not caring a jot about all the disagreements between our powers! I left the island with a friendly farewell and warm memories of birdsong, crystal-clear lakes, the most delicious birch sap and the rustle of thick foliage.

And recently bad news reached me. A giant spider, a vile spawn of the Astral, crept up to the Great Tree under cover of darkness and poisoned it with its venom. All of Dobroslav's followers, and he himself, went mad. Now he is called Zlobinya Yadov, and nothing remains in him of the good-natured sage he once was. Now he and his servants offer blood sacrifices to the Desecrated Tree! The whole island is overrun with venomous spiders tirelessly spawned by their mother, Widixa. And Blackvenom himself hides somewhere in the thick forest. But if you tear out the hearts of the mad pagans and grant them peace by burning them in cleansing fire, Blackvenom will surely not be slow to appear. And with his death the blight will leave the forest forever.

I beg you, cleanse the Desecrated Forest! Kill the Widow and Blackvenom, and perhaps the soul of the one I remember by the name of Dobroslav will find peace...

Bosses: Widixa, Zlobinya Yadov, Yevstigney Volkov, Blackvenom.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest creatures and spirits.

t: A quiet little island, an unremarkable one. Seven hero brothers once lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there, having fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a present: a wondrous mirror, the work of the ancient June, with a golden frame and a glass of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that: from them you can only expect some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it is downright frightening. Although... what if there are hunters willing to get that mirror? For the brave, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

A quiet little island, an inconspicuous one. Seven bogatyr brothers lived there, whiling away their old age among forests and bogs. Then some run-down elven House settled there — they had fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Blight reached the island, then the head of the House brought a little gift for his wife — a Kanian woman, by the way. A wondrous mirror, a work of the ancient June — a golden frame, and the mirror itself of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that: from them you can only expect some trick or curse. In short, there was no reason to call at that island before, and now it's downright frightening. Although... what if there are hunters willing to get that mirror? For the bold, as everyone knows, no law is written!

Bosses: Baba Yaga, Yelisseus, Annette de Tristesse, Evil Mirror.

Climate: Tropical. Closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Elven allod, inhabited by the remnants of the elves whom Catherina drove out.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A quiet little island, an inconspicuous one. Seven bogatyr brothers lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there — they had fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a little present. A marvelous mirror, a work of the ancient June — a golden frame, and the mirror itself of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that — expect nothing from them but some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it's downright frightening. Although... what if there are takers who'll want to get that mirror? For the bold, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

Story allod:

The elves began attacking the shipyard where the new ship "Eclipse" was being built, and generally getting in the way in every manner. The heroes had to be sent to deal with them. The heroes routed the elves, and it turned out that they were led by Alir de Tristesse. That same Alir who had been the head of the minor House of Tristesse and the father of that same Annette who had been Yelisseus's beloved. But the elf's mind had sunk into twilight — he only cried out gloomy prophecies. What had happened stirred Yelisseus himself — he had long searched for his beloved, and it turned out that the elves, on leaving Umoir, had gone to the Drowsy Woods. Without long preparation, Yelisseus set off. Alas, the Drowsy Woods proved a grim place. The Plague was raging there in full force, and nothing remained of the elven settlement but ruins. With a heavy heart Yelisseus found Annette's own diary. It emerged that the elf maiden had fled the persecution of her stepmother, the new wife Alir had brought home. And she had fled into the forest, where she found shelter with seven bogatyrs. Yelisseus set off to find them. When all of them had been found, the brothers told the sad news — Annette had died, killed by the machinations of that same wicked Baba Yaga. Yelisseus set off for revenge and fell into a trap; fortunately the heroes managed to save him and finish off the witch. And the cause, as it turned out, was a June artifact, the Mirror. It remained to say farewell to Annette herself. Yelisseus wished to see his beloved one last time as she lay in a crystal coffin. But when he reached that cave, the coffin was shattered, and out of it stepped Annette... Alas, the elf maiden had become a vampire. Yelisseus was full of resolve to save his beloved after all. "Stop! Don't destroy her!.. So that is what the accursed sorceress meant. Annette, my poor beautiful Annette! It wasn't enough for the witch to destroy the one fairer than she — the mad old woman decided to turn her into a monster! I don't believe it is all fated to end like this. If there is a way in the world to lift the curse from her, I will do it. But I dare not ask you for help again — this is my love and my burden. Leave us. And thank you for everything!"

With heavy hearts the heroes left the cursed island.

Bosses: Baba Yaga, Yelisseus, Annette de Tristesse, Evil Mirror.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Duck River Run is a calm and picturesque place. The folk who live there are simple, warm-hearted and friendly. But here's the trouble — their kindness backfired on them. When an orc gang attacked the island, the locals could not fight them off.

Those bandits are from the Empire. Each of them faced a term in the camps back home, so they stole a ship and took flight. So replenishing supplies off the shores of Duck River Run is no longer safe.

Bosses: Torch the Daring, Haze the Daring, Rod the Daring, Chopper the Daring.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, where Imperial outlaws have settled.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know about that island. How could I not? A decent little place... If you're ready to put up with quacking that doesn't stop for a minute! There's a Kanian village there, and every house has ducks beyond counting. They salt duck, bake it, dry it and sell it. Even the pillow in my cabin is stuffed with local down. It's like lying down to sleep on a cloud... But a misfortune has befallen them. Have you heard about the recent escape from the maximum security zone? No? Strange... It was in all the papers. A whole gang of convicts, mostly orcs and goblins, slaughtered the guards, seized a ship and made off in an unknown direction. They called themselves the "Tribe of the Daring" and set about robbing, wrecking and burning everything in their path. Lawless thugs, what else can I say. They boarded several of our ships, robbed them down to the last frame, and threw the crews overboard. They wiped out an outpost in the far astral root and branch — the Committee's investigators came back from there green as frogs and swearing like cobblers. And the last thing I heard about that gang is that they stumbled upon Duck River Run. Well, the locals are out of luck. I'm afraid even to imagine what lawlessness is going on there now!

Bosses: Torch the Daring, Haze the Daring, Rod the Daring, Chopper the Daring.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
And the accursed Architects were never fully dealt with. The main attack was beaten back with the greatest effort, but at one point those creatures scattered all over the world. And then a captain I know told me — he saw a familiar island in the deep astral, once green as green could be, a real oasis. Now it's bare as a bone. Only those blue spires sticking up. And beasts living there. They look at you with dead eyes. Great eyes glowing blue. Ugh, it gives me the creeps… The Architects must have settled there and are remaking everything in their own wretched likeness again. Oh, if only someone would smash them to pieces…

Bosses: Pteros, Oculus, Arctus, Zero.

Climate: Wasteland, part of the Architects' universe.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Architects.

Story:

And they never did manage to finish off the damned Architects. The main attack was broken with the greatest effort, but at one moment those creatures scattered all over the world. Then a captain I know told me: he saw a familiar island in the deep Astral, once so very green, a real oasis. Now it is stark naked. Only those blue spires stick out. And beasts live there. They stare with a dead gaze. Their big eyes glow blue. Ugh, it gives me goosebumps… The Architects must have settled there and are remaking everything again in their own wretched likeness. Oh, if only someone would smash them to pieces…

Bosses: Pteros, Oculus, Arctus, Zero.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Don't you know? "Where to? To East Overshoe!" — that's how merchants used to answer anyone too curious before casting off from the pier. And not without reason — on East Overshoe there was a rich trading town whose inhabitants, you might say, spoke in nothing but sayings. Whatever you asked a local, he'd answer you with a proverb.

A rich town it was, and misfortune passed it by. The townsfolk got so used to a quiet life that they would say, "we'll start shutting the gates when the crayfish whistles on the mountain." Well, the crayfish held out and held out, and then it whistled. They got what they asked for. And they had been told — let sleeping trouble lie!

I flew past East Overshoe the other day — everything has fallen into desolation, not a sound, not a rustle. But who knows what is really going on there? From afar it's just an abandoned town, but, as they say, still waters run deep!

Bosses: Sleeping Trouble, Clop, Byak and Zyrk, the Noon Witch, Raak.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a large trading city.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't you know? "Where to, where to... To East Overshoe!" — that is how traders used to answer anyone too curious before casting off from the pier. And not without reason — on East Overshoe there was a rich trading city whose inhabitants talked in practically nothing but proverbs. Whatever you ask an Overshoer, he answers you with a saying. It was a rich city, and misfortune passed it by. The Overshoers grew so used to a quiet life that they would say, "we'll start shutting the gates when a crayfish whistles on the mountain". Well, the crayfish waited and waited, and then it whistled. They got what they bargained for. And yet they had been told — let sleeping trouble lie! The other day I flew past East Overshoe — everything has fallen into desolation, not a sound, not a rustle. But who knows what is really going on there? From afar it's just an abandoned city, but, as the saying goes, still waters run deep and devils live in them!

Bosses: Sleeping Trouble, Clop, Byak and Zyrk, the Noon Witch, Raak.

Type: Medium allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Now there is a truly interesting place! There are no end of rumours about the Emerald Isle. Some say it is ruled by the Great Mage Dobrinya Velikov, who has no equal and never has had. He lives in a castle of green gems and can grant any wish. Others tell of a strange company who sought out the mage long ago: a girl named Alla, a Scarecrow, a Talking Lion and an Iron Golem.

Still others retort that it is all just dust in the eyes. Dobrinya is a charlatan, and he was never blessed with any talent but cunning.

Bosses: Brainless Scarecrow, Steel Lumberjack, Cowardly Lion, Dobrinya Velikov.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

There is nothing remarkable about that island. I don't really know much about it. It seems to be a Kanian allod. It is ruled by the illusionist mage Dobrinya Velikov. He calls himself "the Great", though I doubt his strength would really be enough to hold the island. A disagreeable person, I must say... He puffs himself up as if he really were Great, but in fact he is an ordinary fairground conjurer! There is a story that long, long ago a young sorceress, Alla by name, somehow got to that island without any ship at all. A magic whirlwind picked up her house, apparently, and threw it straight there. Along with her little dog and her nail file... There, on the island, Alla met strange but friendly creatures: a talking lion, an ancient lumberjack golem and a living scarecrow. Together with her new friends, having gone through incredible adventures, Alla finally reached the local mage, and he sent the hapless enchantress home. Although personally I suspect that the cause of that journey was not a whirlwind but a bottle of fortified liqueur and the great impressionability of that scatterbrained person, as well as the appetite for sensations of certain chatty scribblers!

Bosses: Brainless Scarecrow, Steel Lumberjack, Cowardly Lion, Dobrinya Velikov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Varied (temperate and wasteland), closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a research base is located here.

Story:

We are met by the base staff, who mention a distress signal in passing but immediately get down to business. Demons have attacked the allod; the base personnel are fighting, but without reinforcements they won't hold out long. An employee tells us, in spite of the secrecy of all the base's work, that a Zem burial has been found on the allod, and that it appeared later than Tep's Plague; as they found out in the course of their research, these Zem turned out to be followers of Tep. During the battle at Asee-Teph the protection fell, and the followers took their secrets to the grave — and it was those that we were looking for. We must find Yaver Matez, the chief Zem scientist at this base, with the help of a Mentaloscope. Making our way past aggressively disposed personnel, we find the scientist. Yaver told us that, according to his theory, the demons are hunting for Tep's knowledge. We must defeat the demon mentors who are trying to extract information from Tep's dead followers. We kill them, and all that remains is to destroy their leader, the Astral Worm.

Bosses: Astral Worm.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Isle of the Edge.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace anywhere? But, believe it or not, there is such a place! It is called Enoch Isle. Once Enoch was a backwater islet of two villages. And then, not so long ago, vampires who had renounced their creator, Armando de Doucer, arrived on the island. Somehow they came to an agreement with the peasants, and they receive blood in exchange for their goods, healing magic and other useful things. You won't believe it, but I saw with my own eyes that people and vampires live in perfect harmony! But everything changed when werewolves appeared on Enoch. A savage pack of half-intelligent beasts invaded Enoch, and peaceful life came to an end. Their leader, the former bandit chieftain Lyut the Bobtailed, has sworn to devour everyone who does not bow before him. The vampires have shut themselves off from the werewolves with magical barriers, closing the passages between the villages, and together with the peasants they are holding back the monsters' attacks with the last of their strength. So if your adventures take you to Enoch, prepare for a fierce battle! Until you manage to completely clear both villages of werewolves, you will not reach their leader.

Bosses: Murk, Paul de Doucer, Vasilissa the Terrible, Lyut the Bobtailed.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Kanian allod, though vampires of the House de Doucer have settled there alongside the Kanians.

Story:

And not so long ago vampires who had renounced their creator, Armando de Doucer, arrived on the island. Somehow they came to an agreement with the peasants and receive blood in exchange for their goods, healing magic and other useful things. You won't believe it, but I saw with my own eyes that people and vampires live there in perfect harmony! But everything changed when werewolves appeared on Enoch. A cruel pack of half-sentient beasts invaded Enoch, and peaceful life came to an end. Their leader, the former bandit chieftain Lyut the Bobtailed, swore to devour everyone who does not bow before him. The vampires shut themselves off from the werewolves with magical barriers, closing the passages between the villages, and together with the peasants they hold back the monsters' attacks with their last strength. So if your adventures take you to Enoch, get ready for a fierce battle! Until you manage to clear both villages of werewolves completely, you will not get to their leader.

Bosses: Murk, Paul de Doucer, Vasilissa the Terrible, Lyut the Bobtailed.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

t:
A distant and inaccessible cloister — the dream of every bachelor in Sarnaut. And no wonder, since this allod is inhabited exclusively by maidens, every one of them clever and beautiful. Seekers of romantic adventure should be careful, though. The beauties fled to Fenia's Cloister in search of a calm and quiet life, so they welcome guests very reluctantly.

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Fenia's Island? Ah, that's the old Kanian fortress where those... what do you call them... right, I remember — the feminists! Or femmeists? Anyway, they're women who believe men wrong and oppress them, which has driven them clean out of their minds. No, you tell me — does anyone wrong women in the Empire? It's in the League that folk are completely savage; they even have a saying there, "a hen's no bird, and a woman's no person." Whereas with us she's every bit a person! Only our Imperial ladies run off to that Cloister regularly too... I don't understand why they've turned so against men?! Well, never mind, listen further. Their leader is some Fenia, a mad sorceress who proclaimed herself a goddess incarnate and the patroness of women. She announced that all the evil in the world comes from men, and decided to wage a merciless war on us — on men, that is! And the funniest thing is that some cracked heads actually believed her! Or rather, it was funny right up until they killed every man on the island, and the parts of their bodies — well, the ones that matter most to a man — they... All right, I don't want to talk about it. A friend of mine, Afanasy Nikitov, was there and saw it all with his own eyes. The horrors he told me... He escaped by a miracle! In short, there are no men in the Cloister now. Instead there's a crowd of women of every race, gone feral for lack of male attention and fanatical to the marrow, ready to tear apart any man who ends up on the island. Now there's a paradox — they hate men, yet without men they turn into beasts. No, I'll never understand women. Especially women who reach for a sword at the slightest thing and try to lop off what's most precious. Ahem. I meant the head, actually, not what you were thinking!

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by ogres and elemental spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Ah, Firefrost and its temple... An island where bitter cold and scorching flame exist in peace and harmony. A beautiful place! And everything that looks beautiful in the Astral is in fact deadly dangerous. I advise you to remember that, and to give Firefrost a wide berth. Before, only wild goblins and trolls lived there, but now, they say, the island has also been overrun by elementals. The cause, I suppose, is the recent eruption of a volcano long thought extinct. And they also say that over all of them stands a mysterious spirit, born of the two elements. I'd like to have a look at that marvel! In short, if you're not afraid of elementals and have no wish to live forever, you can find yourself a sturdy crew and give them battle. After all, it is an ancient temple, and countless riches must surely be hidden in it. It would be a sin to let such goods go to waste!

Bosses: Hestia, Bedlam, Blinder, Diamond.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
The Forgotten Temple? And what, may I ask, has drawn your interest to that accursed place? Believe me, anyone who ends up there will want to forget the nightmares they lived through as quickly as possible. Once it was a heap of June ruins of no interest to anyone, in the middle of an islet of no interest even to demons, but then the Wormfaces reached the temple and awoke the flame that had slumbered in it for centuries. The island blazed like a torch until, by a whim of fate, it collided with an icy fragment of another island. Now half of the island on which the temple stands breathes fire, while on the other half you can freeze to the bone. On top of that it is full of aggressive elementals, old but still working sentry golems, and Wormfaces who greatly dislike strangers. Still, there are madmen among the Historians ready to risk their lives for knowledge. I heard that an expedition led by Martin de Blizare recently set out for the Forgotten Temple... And nobody has heard of that expedition since!

Bosses: Glacier, Ekaterina Arhivina, Sleepless Guard, Az and Yaz.

Climate: Temperate and tundra; the allod consists of four shards.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by elemental spirits and the June.

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

t:
Far out in the Astral I once happened upon an island where eternal winter reigns. It is ruled by Yaver Arteia, a mad Arisen woman who calls herself the Snow Queen. Oh, what a vile hag she is, I tell you! I escaped from that island by a sheer miracle. The Snow Queen's favorite pastime is to abduct people and set them all manner of riddles. Fail to guess one, and you are turned into an ice statue! In her ice castle Yaver Arteia keeps whole galleries of ice sculptures that were once orcs, gibberlings, Arisen, humans... Her heart is as cold as her icy throne!

That merciless shrew was all set to turn me into an ice statue, and only by a miracle did I get away.

Yaver Arteia must be stopped! If she simply killed people, fine — you'd rest a while in Purgatory, and that's that. But she turns them into statues. Just imagine: a man stands there, unable to move, to breathe, even to close his eyes. And so for a year, two, ten... Brr, how horrible. No, such cold-blooded torment cannot go unpunished!

But reaching the queen will not be easy. Chill, a mad werebear shaman, faithfully guards his mistress's peace. And rumor has it that in especially fierce blizzards a huge bear named Helad appears on the island — though whether that is true, it will be up to you to find out.

Bosses: Helad, Sharptooth, Chill, Yaver Arteia.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by trolls and lamias.

t:
What do you think of goblins?

On the one hand — pitiful creatures. Everyone laughs at them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you simply feel sorry for them.

And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Mischief-makers, always ready to do something vile. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on the Coba Plateau? There you go!

There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect one of those, what's it called... such a funny word... a president! For three terms in a row now a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids.

If in your wanderings you manage to find that island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

Bosses: Goblin Overseer, Buzz, Urub.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a goblin settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do you think of goblins? On the one hand, they are unfortunate creatures. Everyone makes fun of them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you just feel sorry for them. And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Nasty pests, always ready to do something low. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on Coba Plateau? There you go! There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect themselves this, what's it called... such a funny word... a president every year! For three terms running a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids. If in the course of your wanderings you manage to find this island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

The island was supposed to be populated entirely by hostile goblins, with no quests and no friendly NPCs.

But it was found without NPCs or monsters... It is mentioned on the astral island Drought (Waters of the Great Canyon).

t:
Climate: Tundra. Closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.

Story:

We are met by the Fearless Family of Gibberlings. They told us that they were sent here by an elder from the Frozen Frontier to find some blood artifact that Nordrak needs so badly. It should be somewhere near the grave of the great June dragon hunter Yad-Volk (he imprisoned Nordrak on the Frozen Frontier). Along the way we try to solve the riddle of the grave: on one of the obelisks a wolf is drawn, and next to it two stones with patterns — and it is these we seek out. The first stone drops from the Yeti Leader, the second is carried by the Harpy Chieftainess. We insert these stones into the hollows of the obelisk in the center of the allod. In a snowstorm Yad-Volk and a Ghostly Dragon appear. After the victory over the dragon, we take the blood artifact from the stele and give it to the Gibberlings.

Bosses: Polar Yeti Leader, Rock Harpy Chieftainess, Ghostly Dragon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Whirl.

t:
It resembles Asee-Teph.

We meet an unknown Elf, who introduces himself as a hero with many feats to his name (he is lying shamelessly), sent by the Conclave of Great Mages to obtain dragon blood. He proposes that we team up and, before setting out on the job, asks us to practise on a draconid. We make our way to the cave with the dragon and kill it. The Elf thanks us for the help and shows off, saying that one day we too will become as famous as he is.

[Map missing]

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph and the Dragon Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by draconids.

Story:

On the island we meet a mysterious individual who tells us about his supposed exploits and says that his task is to obtain the blood of the Great Dragon. He asks us to get some practice before we go after the Great Dragon together with him, and to clear the island of draconids, killing their leader in the process. When we return victorious, the Mysterious Individual says that while we were resting and amusing ourselves with the draconids, he found out that the Great Dragon is in a cave on the other end of the island, and it is time to finish him off. After the victory, the Mysterious Individual says that we did well to defeat the Dragon, and that he, too, started out with exploits just like these and is now a great hero. In a word, showing off.

Bosses: Draconid Boss, Dragon (great).

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Oh, I wouldn't advise you to get mixed up with the draconids. Dangerous creatures. Even the demon hunters who have made an alliance with them do not fully trust these beings. And why? Because the draconids guard their secrets like the apple of their eye! And they do not trust them even to their friends.

I do not know what secret is kept in the Green Maze. The Historians who tried to explore it never managed to get into its far part, access to which is closed off by a magical barrier. As soon as they tried to get past it, two supreme draconids appeared — two Guardians of the Limit, as they call themselves — and drove the Historians out. Since then the draconids greet all uninvited guests with steel.

If risk is to your taste, you can try to uncover the secret of the Green Maze. But you will have to find your own way through the ancient ruins.

Bosses: Version 1: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Cursed Warrior. Version 2: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Reborn Warrior, Twice Born.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

t:
Have you ever heard of Volcano Isle? No? Then listen. Not long ago a tribe of draconids appeared on this island, worshipping a fire god who sleeps in the crater of a long-extinct volcano. With constant sacrifices the draconids kept him asleep, so that he would not awaken and his scorching fury would not break loose. But not long ago their high priest broke with custom and summoned the sleeper. The volcano awoke, and a mighty fire elemental burst out. From tongues of flame and the heat of flowing magma he created four guardians — huge fiery manticores whose breath can burn anyone to ashes on the spot! If you decide to go to the island and try to awaken the sleeping flame, you must repeat the draconids' ritual, laying the fiery hearts of shellbacks on the sacrificial altars. But don't even try to take him on while his faithful manticores are alive! The fire god put a particle of his power into each guardian, and with their deaths he will be greatly weakened. That's all I know about Volcano Isle. Good luck to you!

Bosses: Supreme Draconid, Bonesnapper, Hephaesto.

Climate: Tropical. Closest to the Kingdom of Elements.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by fire elementals and draconids.

t:
And how do you know about that, eh?

That's classified information! The Committee will wring your neck for divulging it!

Oh, all right. Since you already know about the heretics themselves, so be it — I'll share it with you in secret. But mind you, not a word to anyone!

The Heretic Refuge is a stain on the reputation of all the Arisen. After all, it is from their people that all these dangerous madmen come!

The heretics refuse to recognize the holiness of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believe that all that exists arose from four elements — fire, earth, water, and nature as the union of all three pure elements. And they have grown so hidebound in their heresy that they accept no arguments of reason. They fiercely hate everyone who does not share their faith. After several high-profile murders committed by this sect, the Church, with the full support of the Committee and of Yasker himself, anathematized them and opened a hunt for them.

The heretics — or rather, the handful that was left of their sect — seized an astral ship in port and vanished into the depths of the Astral. Time passed, and their existence was simply forgotten; all the documents were classified and handed over to the archive. And not long ago a captain I know told me he had heard about the heretics from someone who had seen with his own eyes a man who had the misfortune to stumble upon their refuge in the Astral. That poor wretch barely escaped! His ship was scorched by fire, a gaping hole from a huge boulder yawned in the hold, all the rigging was covered in mold, and half the crew had turned into ice statues...

So if your adventures lead you to the secret refuge of the heretics, know this — they are mad killers, and they will try to destroy you at any cost!

Bosses: Yasskul Flach, Negus Minhotep, Negus Haifa, Negus Zirach.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Zem fanatics and heretics.

t:
I've never had occasion to visit the Edge island.

It got its name because it often appears near the Holy Land. No wonder the League and the Empire sought to seize it to use as an additional base. Our side proved quicker.

But now access to the island is forbidden. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Edge has betrayed the Empire! Evidently there were demon cultists among them who managed to cloud the soldiers' minds. Or perhaps the whole thing is down to the astral worm that has dug in in the middle of the island. They say it can have a destructive effect on the mind.

Elizaveta Rysina herself recently summoned me and questioned me about the heroes of the Empire. The thing is, our side currently has no way to send a punitive expedition to the island. And yet the traitors must be punished! And the island cleansed of demons!

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a research base.

t:
If you open a primer at the letter "K" (for krepost, "fortress"), you can see a fortress surrounded by a sturdy stone wall. That picture appeared long, long ago, and as his model the artist used the Hunters' Stockade — an exemplary defensive structure of those times. It was built before the Cataclysm, when the Abatis Line was being laid — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids.

After the catastrophe the fortress vanished into the Astral along with other shards of the old world.

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a demon hunters' base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

It's an ancient fortress, a venerable one. His-to-ri-cal! The Kanians built it even before the Cataclysm, when they were laying the Abatis Line — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids. How many times it was besieged, how many times burnt to the ground — and every time it was rebuilt. So it stood right up until the catastrophe, and then, together with other shards of the old world, it was lost in the Astral. And now, centuries later, the Demon Hunters found it — dilapidated, but all in one piece. Some say it was the courage of many generations of defenders that preserved it, others insist on an astral anomaly... Be that as it may, the Hunters rebuilt it, reinforced it with meteorite shards and turned it into one of their most powerful strongholds. Demons are afraid to sail within cannon shot of it!

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
A strange little place... Maybe that island truly exists, maybe it's a mirage, a phantasm, a glamour. The island is covered in thick forests and deep bogs. All sorts of creatures live there, some intelligent, some you couldn't really call that. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And above all — there are hordes of ghosts there! Kanians mostly, sort of alive and sort of not. And they all obey the mistress of the place — Ziva, I think she's called — whether she's a woman, a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful place; the mistress was kind to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I've heard from other travelers that some misfortune befell it recently — an unhappy love, or some curse... In short, I'd think twice before mooring at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons.

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest creatures and nature spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A strange little place... Either that island really exists, or it is a mirage, a phantom, a delusion. That island is covered with dense forests and deep swamps. All sorts of creatures live there, some sentient and some not so much. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And most importantly — there are ghosts there without number! Mostly Kanians, seemingly alive and yet not. And they all obey the mistress of that place, Ziva is her name, I think — whether a human, or a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful little place; the mistress was welcoming to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I heard from other travellers that some misfortune happened there recently — whether an unhappy love or some curse... In short, I would think twice about putting in at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons!

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Long ago honest folk jokingly called one distant district the Far-Far-Away Kingdom. It was a real backwater: a rider couldn't get through, nor a man on foot. A wall of trees — for hundreds of versts! And this land was ruled by a wise guardian — the living soul of the forest. She did not favor wicked travelers, but for good ones the path through the thicket unrolled of its own accord.

After the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. And the guardian, they say, survived — she watches over her domain as in the old days. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the ancient trees. But Light forbid anyone should harm the local animals! It is said more than one poachers' vessel has vanished without a trace near the Isle of Far-Far-Away!

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest fauna and spirits.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Isle of Far-Far-Away? Hm... As an acquaintance of mine put it: "Calm, smooth, and the grace of Tensess." And where does such a strange name come from? Well, it's a funny story. Long ago, before the Cataclysm, one remote Kanian province had a name so jaw-breaking that it wasn't preserved even in official charters. And the inhabitants themselves jokingly called their land the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was a real backwater... Forest, forest and nothing but forest! Thousands of hectares of solid green. And it was ruled by a guardian — the living soul of the forest. They say whoever entered that forest with ill thoughts never came out again. Well, after the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. But it held out and did not melt away in the astral. And the guardian, they say, survived too. Knowledgeable people told me that her magic still protects the island. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the age-old trees. But Light forbid you anger the mistress of the forest! If you try to turn the local animals into shashlik, you won't have time to blink before you're turned into cutlets yourself.

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
